podcast.body: Released in 1988 under the alias The Timelords, this acid house anthem famously sampled Delia Derbyshire's "Doctor Who Theme" and Gary Glitter's "Rock and Roll Part 2." The track's availability is limited, partly due to Gary Glitter's disgraced status and the KLF's anti-copyright philosophy, expressed in their name "Copyright Liberation Front." "The KLF working as the Timewords in 1988 and Dr. In The Tartus, which takes Delia Derbyshire's version of the Dr. Who theme and melds it with Gary Glitter's Rock and Roll Part 2."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1988 under their alias The Timewords, this acid house anthem by The KLF ingeniously combines Delia Derbyshire's electronic version of the "Doctor Who" theme with Gary Glitter's "Rock and Roll Part 2." However, due to Gary Glitter's disgraced status as a convicted pedophile and The KLF's practice of not clearing samples, this song is not available on platforms like iTunes. "The KLF, working as the Timewords in 1988 and Dr. In The Tartus, which takes Delia Derbyshire's version of The Dr. Who theme and melds it with Gary Glitter's Rock and Roll Part 2."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
